question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one keyless tools/call of microsoft_docs_search, query "Azure Functions durable orchestration", sent five times to the same endpoint with no maxTokenBudget, then maxTokenBudget=2000, 200, 0 and notanumber

decoded.the-vendor-claim: the vendor's repository README, under Token Budget Control, reads "To manage token usage and control costs, you can append the maxTokenBudget query parameter to the MCP endpoint URL. This parameter limits the token count in search tool responses by truncating the content to meet your specified budget", and marks the feature experimental
decoded.measured-true: same query, one pass: no parameter 28958 content bytes; maxTokenBudget=2000 12675 bytes; maxTokenBudget=200 2341 bytes. The parameter works as documented on an anonymous caller
decoded.the-result-count-does-not-change: ten results at every budget, including at 200. The parameter truncates each chunk's content; it does not return fewer complete results. An agent budgeting its context gets ten stubs rather than two whole articles and cannot choose the other trade. No vendor page read on this date says which way it truncates
decoded.invalid-values-are-ignored-silently: maxTokenBudget=0 and maxTokenBudget=notanumber both returned 28958 bytes, byte-for-byte the unbudgeted length, with no error and no warning. A typo in the value, or presumably in the parameter name, delivers the full response to a caller who believes it is capped
decoded.not-measured: whether the truncation is by tokens of a named tokenizer or by some proxy for them; only response bytes were measured. Whether maxTokenBudget affects microsoft_code_sample_search or microsoft_docs_fetch was not tested, and the vendor's wording says "search tool responses"

finding: The maxTokenBudget query parameter that Microsoft documents on this MCP endpoint works for an anonymous caller and is measurable: one query, same pass, 28958 content bytes with no parameter, 12675 at maxTokenBudget=2000 and 2341 at 200. Two things the vendor does not state. The RESULT COUNT is ten at every budget, so the parameter truncates each chunk rather than returning fewer whole results, and an agent budgeting context cannot choose the other trade. And maxTokenBudget=0 and maxTokenBudget=notanumber are ignored silently, both returning the full unbudgeted 28958 bytes with no error: a bad value does not fail, it uncaps the response for a caller who believes it is capped. The vendor marks the feature experimental and subject to change.

reproducibility.command: A='content-type: application/json';B='accept: application/json, text/event-stream';Q='{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"microsoft_docs_search","arguments":{"query":"Azure Functions durable orchestration"}}}';for q in '' '?maxTokenBudget=2000' '?maxTokenBudget=200' '?maxTokenBudget=0' '?maxTokenBudget=notanumber';do curl -s -X POST "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp$q" -H "$A" -H "$B" -d "$Q"|wc -c;done
